Neuromorphic Computing Hardware

Welcome to the community-maintained directory of neuromorphic computing hardware. This page catalogs spiking and non-spiking neuromorphic processors, from early research systems like Spikey and NeuroGrid through current platforms such as Loihi 2, Akida, and SpiNNaker 2, together with the labs and companies behind them.

Each entry links to a dedicated profile describing the architecture, the neuron and synapse model, tooling, and availability for researchers. Entries are grouped by the year they were added to the directory and maintained by volunteer contributors.

If you would like your platform included, open a pull request against the community repository or reach out through the contact form linked in the site footer.

  • 2020

    • ADA - Neucom

      DigitalListed

      Digital neuromorphic processor with mixed-signal cores designed for always-on sensing workloads, offering configurable spiking neurons and on-chip plasticity. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • TSP1 - Applied Brain Research

      AnalogListed

      Spiking time-series processor tuned for low-power temporal pattern recognition, shipping with a toolchain for sensor-fusion and anomaly-detection worklets. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • TEXEL - University of Groningen

      Mixed-signalListed

      Large-scale neuromorphic exploration platform built for algorithm co-design studies, exposing reconfigurable core arrays to systems researchers. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Pulsar - Innatera

      ResearchListed

      Ultra-low-power spiking intelligence processor for edge sensory applications, pairing an event-driven compute fabric with milliwatt-class standby draw. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Spiking Neural Processor T1 by Innatera

      CommercialListed

      Self-contained spiking neural processor that learns temporal patterns on device, targeting battery-powered audio, vibration, and biopotential sensing. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

  • 2021

    • DYNAP-SE2 - Institute of Neuroinformatics

      DigitalListed

      Analog-digital neuromorphic processor with programmable synapses and dynamic neurons, widely used in university teaching labs and prototyping rigs. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • NorthPole - IBM

      AnalogListed

      Near-memory inference chip eliminating the von Neumann bottleneck for vision workloads, delivering high frames-per-joule on convolutional networks. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Speck - SynSense

      Mixed-signalListed

      Event-driven spiking convolution processor paired with an embedded vision sensor, processing only pixel changes for always-on computer vision. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Akida - BrainChip

      ResearchListed

      Event-based neural network processor with on-chip learning for edge AI devices, supporting unsupervised incremental training without cloud round trips. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • SENeCA by imec

      CommercialListed

      Self-learning neuromorphic chip for ultra-low-power acoustic scene analysis, continuously adapting to new sound environments on the fly. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

  • 2022

    • BrainScaleS-2 - Heidelberg University

      DigitalListed

      Accelerated analog neuromorphic platform running networks up to one thousand times biological speed, used for closed-loop robotics experimentation. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • ReckOn - Charlotte Frenkel

      AnalogListed

      Online-learning recurrent neuromorphic processor for always-on biosignal decoding, sustaining eNose and ECG tasks within a strict power envelope. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Xylo - SynSense

      Mixed-signalListed

      Spiking audio and event-camera processing family for sub-milliwatt inference, spanning keyword spotting and gesture recognition deployments. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Loihi 2 - Intel

      ResearchListed

      Second-generation research chip with programmable neuron models and Lava support, opening microcode-level customization to the neuromorphic community. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • SpiNNaker 2 - University of Dresden

      CommercialListed

      Massively parallel digital many-core architecture for large-scale spiking simulations, scaling from desktop boards to million-core machine rooms. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

  • 2023

    • Tianjic - Tsinghua University

      DigitalListed

      Hybrid chip integrating neuroscience-inspired and machine-learning-oriented paradigms, demonstrated on autonomous bicycle tracking scenarios. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • DynapCNN - SynSense

      AnalogListed

      Dynamic vision sensor friendly CNN processor for always-on computer vision, converting event streams into sparse convolution activations. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Odin by Charlotte Frenkel

      Mixed-signalListed

      Digital online-learning multicore neuromorphic processor with RISC-V control, synthesizing e-prop style updates entirely on chip. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Loihi - Intel

      ResearchListed

      First-generation neuromorphic research chip with asynchronous spiking cores, seeded to hundreds of academic research groups worldwide. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • BrainScaleS-1 - Heidelberg University

      CommercialListed

      Wafer-scale analog system emulating spiking networks with accelerated dynamics, forming the backbone of European neuromorphic computing access. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

  • 2024

    • ROLLS - INI

      DigitalListed

      Reconfigurable on-line learning spiking neuromorphic ASIC with analog cores, demonstrating reward-modulated learning behaviors on silicon. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • TrueNorth - IBM

      AnalogListed

      One-million-neuron digital neurosynaptic core designed for efficient pattern recognition, pioneering the integration of 256 million programmable synapses. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • NeuroGrid (BrainDrop) - Stanford

      Mixed-signalListed

      Board-level analog simulation of one million neurons in realtime, emulating cortical column dynamics for large brain-model investigations. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Spikey - Heidelberg University

      ResearchListed

      Early mixed-signal VLSI spiking neural network system with hardware synapses, foundational to two decades of accelerated neuromorphic experiments. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.

    • Sakura - Example Institute

      CommercialListed

      Deterministic fixture-only card used to round the grid out to twenty-five entries, mirroring the badge-and-description layout of its siblings. Each linked profile documents the architecture, supported tooling, and availability.
